findings.reason: Verified in googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse wrapper, and line 100 stores it as data: { key }, so the stored key is {success, data} and the next googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) fails on every install.

Computed keys like [z.string().toString()] produce "[object Object]" (zod's default toString), so the sync-mode schema drops expiry fields such as expires_in and instance_url through z.object's default stripping; the claim holds but only affects the opt-in sync path.
In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, so Google's res?.data and Zoho's .data.error read undefined and throw a TypeError; real but limited to the opt-in sync path.

Verified in zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts: credentialId (credential.id) is passed as the third argument, which the helper sends as calcomUserId, so the sync endpoint is asked for the wrong user's tokens when sync is enabled.

Verified: salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts has no prisma import (only one reference, at line 96), so prisma.credential.update is a ReferenceError or type error on every Salesforce client construction.

Verified in the salesforce getClient: a token refresh runs on every construction with no expiry check, and the jsforce Connection is built from the old credentialKey.access_token, which may already be expired; the fragile statusText check is also real.
An unhandled parse or decrypt throw gives a generic 500, a minor error-handling gap with no concrete security or data impact.

A non-constant-time string comparison on a network webhook secret is a marginal hardening point; the endpoint is also gated by the sharing-enabled check, and timing exploitation over HTTP is impractical.
